A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpeedCP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The retained material and relocated experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic simulations and experiments on molecular property prediction, arXiv citation prediction, and brain tumor MRI, including coverage, prediction-set size, and runtime.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds neural-network predictor results and several sensitivity, tuning, and computational analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes hyperparameter tuning from calibration data to a separate, disjoint Dsplit. This revises the proposed procedure, while retaining the RKHS objective, embeddings, solution paths, and randomized cutoff. V2 explicitly states that its main experiments still tune on calibration data.

E1.justification: The real-world datasets and tasks remain unchanged; arXiv moves to Appendix D.2.1. New elbow-size experiments extend synthetic coverage to different Dirichlet distributions, including stronger covariate shift, and different clusterwise label-noise regimes (D.1.7).

E2.justification: SplitCP appears in v1's synthetic Figure 2 and Table 4 but is omitted from the corresponding linear-predictor Figure 2 and Table 1 in v2. It remains in other comparisons, including v2's neural-network Figure 5. CondCP, PCP, and RLCP remain comparators.

E3.justification: The stated synthetic training/calibration/test split changes from 400/400/200 to 600/300/100. V2 also adds a two-layer neural-network predictor, half-calibration holdout tuning controls, kernel-family comparisons, sample-size sweeps, and evaluation at 25 hyperparameter pairs. These substantially expand the evaluation protocols; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of sample-size dependence, kernel sensitivity, calibration reuse versus separate tuning, hyperparameter sensitivity, cutoff randomization, and elbow sizes and breakpoint counts (D.1.1 and D.1.3–D.1.7). These directly investigate robustness and computational behavior beyond v1's existing feature-map discussion and MRI embedding comparisons.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly reports within-seed variability of randomized cutoffs, and D.1.7 specifies ten independent data generations for the elbow studies. Existing benchmark experiments retain their 50-run reporting. This does not establish increased repetition of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Substantial new outcomes cover neural-network prediction, kernels, tuning, and computational sensitivity. For example, v2 Table 5 reports marginal coverage of 0.893, 0.884, and 0.892 for RBF, Matérn, and IMQ. Synthetic RLCP runtime changes from 0.917±0.11 seconds in v1 Table 4 to 22.05±0.07 in v2 Table 1; revised splits prevent interpreting this as a same-setting change. Molecular, arXiv, and MRI table values are retained.

T1.justification: V2 replaces v1 Theorem 2's alignment-dependent formulation with an oracle theorem and a separate estimated-group Corollary C.3. It adds Lemma C.13's density-dependent, square-root-lambda coverage-gap bound and proof, changes the coverage-gap prefactor in equation 10, and revises path derivations and complexity reasoning. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same central claims: efficient RKHS solution paths, conditional calibration using low-rank embeddings, and finite-sample coverage analysis. The headline empirical claims of roughly 30% shorter intervals and 40-fold speedup also remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges possible coverage distortion from calibration-based tuning and recommends independent tuning when feasible. It develops the locality-versus-stability tradeoff, weak bounds in sparse regions, and limitations as regularization vanishes. It also distinguishes estimated-group from true-group coverage and newly attributes CondCP's conservative results to solver approximations.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.5 details bandwidth cross-validation followed by SIC-based regularization selection; v1 only briefly mentioned SIC. V2 also specifies a GIN predictor and absolute-residual scores for molecular experiments and a 30-hour CondCP timeout for arXiv. Hardware and code-access information remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 elaborates the connection to LARS and existing RKHS path algorithms and adds adaptive-tuning and kernel references, including Efron, Gauthier, Rasmussen–Williams, Stein, and Gorham–Mackey. Li et al.'s influence was already acknowledged in v1's appendix. Publication updates for retained conformal references do not introduce new comparison methods.

P1.justification: V2 polishes explanations, brings related-work discussion into the introduction, moves the arXiv discussion into the appendix, and introduces numbered synthetic-analysis subsections. Author ordering also changes. These reorganize parts of the narrative while preserving the overall main-text and Appendix A–D structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially recomposed with fewer heatmaps, and the molecular coverage panels are divided between main-text Figure 4 and appendix Figure 12. The synthetic summary table gains predictor-specific columns, and multiple new diagnostic plots and sensitivity tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the treatment of central validity and efficiency questions. It distinguishes independently tuned guarantees from calibration reuse, tests that practical departure, separates oracle and estimated-group coverage, and supplies kernel and elbow-size sensitivity evidence absent from v1. These gains outweigh reduced synthetic baseline reporting. Important limitations remain: main experiments still reuse calibration data, and Algorithm 1's joint cross-validation description is not reconciled with Appendix B.5's CV/SIC procedure.
